title: Town-terrorising 'werewolf' connected to UFOs, claims 13-year-long investigation
excerpt: A retired teacher claims a 13-year, data-driven probe into the 'Beast of Bray Road' has unearthed eerie evidence of a 7ft 'werewolf' linked to disturbing UFO-like lights
content:
A retired teacher claims a 13-year, data-driven probe into the 'Beast of Bray Road' has unearthed eerie evidence of a 7ft 'werewolf' linked to disturbing UFO-like lights

12:28, 01 Nov 2026

A “werewolf” has been reportedly terrorising residents in a quiet town. Now, a 13-year investigation has seemingly uncovered a bizarre link to UFOs.

‌

‌

The creature is known as the Beast of Bray Road, a hairy, wolf-like figure said to stalk the lanes around Elkhorn, Wisconsin, USA since the 1980s. Retired teacher Lee Hampel, who owns a 35-acre farm along Bray Road, has spent 13 years compiling what he believes is serious evidence, approaching the mystery with a data-led mindset shaped by his background teaching maths and computer science.

‌

According to an investigative report by NewsNation, Hampel has amassed thousands of files during his long-running probe, including a huge collection of images from motion-activated cameras set up across his land.

‌

He reportedly claims to have gathered more than 100,000 photos across around 200 SD cards using trail cams. Moreover, one of his key pieces of evidence is said to be an iPhone photo showing a dark figure standing near a cornfield.

Hampel says a scale analysis of the image suggested the figure was around 7ft tall with shoulders roughly 3.5ft wide, News Nation reported. If accurate, these measurements would be far larger than a typical wolf or coyote.

Additionally, Hampel reportedly says he has personally seen the beast three times and managed to take plaster casts of its tracks. The prints, he claims, show a massive five-toed, seven-pad footprint that doesn’t match known local wildlife.

‌

He even took one 3.5-inch track to the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, but says they brushed it off as an abnormal coyote. Hampel also admitted he tried to lure the creature out by leaving roadkill - including deer and raccoons - on his property, as per News Nation.

He reportedly claims the carcasses didn’t just disappear, but were found “surgically” gutted and stacked neatly in piles, with no human footprints around to suggest a person was responsible. Hampel now also believes the Beast of Bray Road may be tied to UFO activity after repeatedly noticing strange electronic failures right as the meat vanished.

‌

Rather than capturing clear footage of a predator dragging off heavy carcasses, he claims his cameras recorded unexplained flashing orbs, bright white lights and what he described as a thick “black mist”. He also claims the heavy animals seemed to vanish without triggering motion sensors.

‌

According to Hampel, there are strange objects in the night sky blinking out of existence. “Elkhorn doesn’t like to talk about it, so we don’t really know how often it is seen,” Hampel told the Chicago Tribune.

“But science, of course, is full of unknown things.” He further said: “Maybe in 75 years, we’ll know for sure.

‌

“People will say, ‘Oh, back in 2026, Lee Hampel had all sorts of information on that dogman.’ I have a neighbour who has lived here 50 years, never seen it.

“But he’s seeing all these odd tracks and tells me he doesn’t know what’s making them. Well, I know.

‌

“It’s the Beast of Bray Road!”
